definition: Never-Ending Language Learning (NELL) system is a semantic machine learning system that as of 2010 was being developed by a research team at Carnegie Mellon University, and supported by grants from DARPA, Google, NSF, and CNPq with portions of the system running on a supercomputing cluster provided by Yahoo!.
details: Never-Ending Language Learning (NELL) system is a semantic machine learning system that as of 2010 was being developed by a research team at Carnegie Mellon University, and supported by grants from DARPA, Google, NSF, and CNPq with portions of the system running on a supercomputing cluster provided by Yahoo!.

explainer.lead: Never-Ending Language Learning (NELL) is a semantic machine learning system developed at Carnegie Mellon University that was running as of 2010 with support from DARPA, Google, NSF, and CNPq. It matters as an early effort at continuous, large-scale semantic learning.

tiers.eli5: It's a program that keeps reading and learning facts without being told to stop, like a student who never graduates.
tiers.practitioner: Parts of the system ran on a supercomputing cluster provided by Yahoo!, showing that continuous semantic learning depends on sustained compute; a pitfall is assuming such a system runs without ongoing engineering and infrastructure.
tiers.paperLevel: NELL is a semantic machine learning system developed by a Carnegie Mellon University research team as of 2010, funded by grants from DARPA, Google, NSF, and CNPq, with portions running on a Yahoo!-provided supercomputing cluster.

explainer.example: NELL reads text continuously and accumulates semantic knowledge, with its heavier computation distributed across a Yahoo! cluster.
